name: KPSC / KAS (Karnataka)
description: Karnataka-focused questions for KPSC / KAS: state history, geography, polity and culture.

questions.question: What is the capital of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru has been the capital of Karnataka (earlier Mysore State) since 1956.

questions.question: The famous temples of Belur and Halebidu were built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Hoysalas (10th–14th century) built the star-shaped Chennakeshava (Belur) and Hoysaleshwara (Halebidu) temples — masterpieces of soapstone carving.

questions.question: The Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru is the seat of which institution?
questions.explanation: The Vidhana Soudha houses the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. Built by Kengal Hanumanthaiah, it was completed in 1956.

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Minister of Karnataka (then Mysore State)?
questions.explanation: K. Chengalaraya (K. C.) Reddy became the first Chief Minister of Mysore State in 1947, after independence.

questions.question: The river Kaveri originates from which place in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri hills in Kodagu district and flows ~800 km to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Jog Falls, one of India's highest waterfalls, is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls (253 m) in Shivamogga district is formed by the Sharavati river plunging in four cascades — Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket.

questions.question: Rani Chennamma of Kittur led an armed rebellion in 1824 against whom?
questions.explanation: Kittur Rani Chennamma fought the British East India Company in 1824 against the Doctrine of Lapse annexation — decades before the 1857 revolt.

questions.question: The world-famous Dasara (Nadahabba) festival is celebrated most grandly in which Karnataka city?
questions.explanation: Mysuru Dasara, a 10-day royal festival with the Jamboo Savari procession, has been celebrated for over 400 years under the Wodeyars.

questions.question: What is the official language of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kannada is Karnataka's official language — one of India's classical languages, with over 2,000 years of literary history.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district is most famous for coffee plantations?
questions.explanation: Kodagu (Coorg) is Karnataka's largest coffee-producing district; the state grows ~70% of India's coffee.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by whom?
options: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
questions.explanation: Brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded the empire in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra, guided by saint Vidyaranya.

questions.question: The UNESCO World Heritage ruins of Hampi lie on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, stands on the Tungabhadra river in Vijayanagara district.

questions.question: 'Kavirajamarga', the earliest available Kannada literary work, was composed during the reign of which Rashtrakuta king?
questions.explanation: Written by the poet Srivijaya around 850 CE in the court of Amoghavarsha I (Nrupatunga), 'Kavirajamarga' is a treatise on poetics.

questions.question: Bengaluru city was founded in 1537 by which chieftain?
questions.explanation: Kempe Gowda I, a feudatory of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded Bengaluru in 1537, building its mud fort and petes.

questions.question: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', was the ruler of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan ruled the Kingdom of Mysore (1782–1799) and died defending Srirangapatna in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

questions.question: Which Karnataka city houses the state's major seaport — the New Mangalore Port?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port at Panambur (Mangaluru) is Karnataka's only major port, handling coffee, cashew and crude oil trade.

questions.question: The Gol Gumbaz, famous for its whispering gallery, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura is the mausoleum of Adil Shahi Sultan Mohammed Adil Shah — its dome is among the largest in the world.

questions.question: Karnataka was formed on 1 November 1956. What was the state called before it was renamed in 1973?
questions.explanation: The state was created as Mysore State on 1 November 1956 and renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973 — now celebrated as Kannada Rajyotsava.

questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayyanagiri (1,930 m) in the Baba Budangiri range of Chikkamagaluru district is Karnataka's highest peak.

questions.question: The Halmidi inscription (~450 CE) is famous as what?
options: The earliest Sanskrit work of Karnataka
questions.explanation: Found in Hassan district, the Halmidi inscription is the earliest known full-length Kannada inscription, dating to about 450 CE.

questions.question: The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur (1117 CE) was commissioned during the reign of which Hoysala king?
questions.explanation: King Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur in 1117 CE to commemorate his victory over the Cholas at Talakad.

questions.question: Who was the Maharaja of Mysore when the state acceded to the Indian Union in 1947?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar signed the Instrument of Accession in 1947 and later served as Governor of Madras and Mysore.

questions.question: Which is the largest district of Karnataka by area?
questions.explanation: Belagavi (~13,415 km²) is Karnataka's largest district by area, in the state's northwest bordering Maharashtra and Goa.

questions.question: The Hampi ruins now fall under which district, carved out in 2020?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara district (headquarters Hospete) was carved out of Ballari district in 2020, taking Hampi with it.

questions.question: Who is remembered as 'Karnataka Kulapurohita' — the high priest of the Karnataka unification movement?
questions.explanation: Aluru Venkata Rao's 1917 book 'Karnataka Gatha Vaibhava' inspired the Ekikarana (unification) movement, earning him the title Karnataka Kulapurohita.

questions.question: What is the state tree of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Sandalwood (Santalum album) is Karnataka's state tree — the state is famous for Mysore sandalwood. The state animal is the Asian Elephant.

questions.question: Kudremukh National Park is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh National Park (horse-face peak, 1,894 m) lies in Chikkamagaluru district in the Western Ghats — a UNESCO World Heritage cluster.

questions.question: The Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) dam near Mysuru is built across which river?
questions.explanation: The KRS dam, designed by Sir M. Visvesvaraya and completed in 1932, is built across the Kaveri and created the Brindavan Gardens.

questions.question: Which Kannada poet, author of 'Sri Ramayana Darshanam', is honoured as Karnataka's 'Rashtrakavi' (national poet)?
questions.explanation: Kuvempu (K. V. Puttappa) was the first Kannada Jnanpith awardee (1967) and was named Rashtrakavi; 'Jaya Bharata Jananiya Tanujate' is his anthem.

questions.question: Engineers' Day in India (15 September) honours which Karnataka-born engineer-statesman?
questions.explanation: Sir M. Visvesvaraya (born 15 Sept 1861, Muddenahalli) — KRS dam, Bharat Ratna 1955 — is honoured on Engineers' Day for his contributions.

questions.question: The Badami Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II is remembered for defeating which northern emperor on the Narmada?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II checked Harshavardhana's southward advance at the Narmada, an event recorded in the Aihole inscription. Harsha's expansion stopped there.

questions.question: The Aihole inscription, praising Pulakeshin II, was composed by which court poet?
questions.explanation: Ravikirti composed the Aihole prashasti in Sanskrit. Harisena wrote the comparable Allahabad pillar inscription for Samudragupta, and Pampa and Ranna were later Kannada poets.

questions.question: The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled from which capital?
questions.explanation: The Rashtrakutas ruled from Manyakheta, modern Malkhed in Kalaburagi district. Badami was the Chalukya capital, Dwarasamudra the Hoysala one and Hampi the Vijayanagara one.

questions.question: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, carved from a single rock, was built under which dynasty of Karnataka origin?
questions.explanation: The Rashtrakuta king Krishna I commissioned the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora. The Hoysalas built in soapstone much later and further south.

questions.question: The Kadamba dynasty, among the earliest to rule from Karnataka, had its capital at
questions.explanation: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada was the Kadamba capital, founded by Mayurasharma. Talakadu was a Western Ganga centre and Halebidu the Hoysala capital.

questions.question: The colossal Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola was commissioned by
questions.explanation: Chavundaraya, a Western Ganga minister and commander, had the monolith of Bahubali carved around 981 CE. Vishnuvardhana was a later Hoysala king.

questions.question: Krishnadevaraya, the best-known Vijayanagara emperor, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, the third of the four Vijayanagara lines. Sangama was the founding dynasty and Aravidu the last.

questions.question: The Battle of Talikota in 1565, which broke Vijayanagara power, was fought against
questions.explanation: An alliance of the Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota, after which Hampi was sacked. The Mughals had not yet reached the Deccan in force.

questions.question: Hyder Ali rose to power in Mysore as a commander under which ruling house?
questions.explanation: Hyder Ali served the Wadiyar rulers of Mysore before taking effective control of the kingdom. His son Tipu Sultan succeeded him.

questions.question: Onake Obavva is remembered for defending which fort against Hyder Ali's forces?
questions.explanation: Onake Obavva defended a narrow opening in the Chitradurga fort wall using a pestle. The fort is known for its seven concentric walls.

questions.question: The Keladi or Nayaka rulers of Ikkeri are associated with which region of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Keladi Nayakas ruled the Malnad and coastal tract from Ikkeri and later Bidnur. Queen Chennamma of Keladi famously sheltered Rajaram from the Mughals.

questions.question: The Ekikarana movement in Karnataka campaigned for what?
options: Unification of Kannada-speaking areas into one state
questions.explanation: Ekikarana was the movement to bring Kannada-speaking regions, then scattered across several administrations, into a single state, achieved in 1956.

questions.question: Which is the largest river basin in Karnataka by area within the state?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin covers the largest share of Karnataka, draining the northern districts. The Kaveri basin dominates the south.

questions.question: The Tungabhadra river is formed by the confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra near which town?
questions.explanation: The Tunga and Bhadra meet at Koodli in Shivamogga district to form the Tungabhadra, a major tributary of the Krishna.

questions.question: Which Karnataka region is known as the Malnad?
questions.explanation: Malnad means hill country and refers to the Western Ghats belt of high rainfall and dense forest. The coastal strip is Karavali and the interior plateau Bayaluseeme.

questions.question: Karnataka's coastal region is commonly known as
questions.explanation: Karavali is the coastal belt covering Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada. Malnad is the hill country inland of it.

questions.question: The Kolar region of Karnataka was historically famous for mining which mineral?
questions.explanation: The Kolar Gold Fields were among the deepest gold mines in the world before closing in 2001. Ballari and Chitradurga are the iron ore districts instead.

questions.question: The Sharavathi river drains into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Sharavathi is a west-flowing river reaching the Arabian Sea near Honnavar, plunging over Jog Falls on the way. The Kaveri and Krishna flow east.

questions.question: Bandipur National Park, a tiger reserve in Karnataka, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Bandipur lies in Chamarajanagar district, adjoining Nagarhole in Karnataka and Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu as part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district is the leading producer of iron ore?
questions.explanation: Ballari is Karnataka's principal iron ore district, with Chitradurga and Tumakuru also significant. Kodagu and Mandya are agricultural districts.

questions.question: The Deccan plateau region of northern Karnataka is drained mainly by which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Krishna and its tributary the Bhima drain the northern Karnataka plateau. The Netravati and Gurupura are short coastal rivers near Mangaluru.

questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the state of Karnataka?
options: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President, while the Chief Minister heads the elected government and exercises real executive power.

questions.question: The High Court of Karnataka has its principal seat at which city?
questions.explanation: The principal seat is at Bengaluru, with permanent benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi to serve the northern districts.

questions.question: How many seats does Karnataka have in the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Karnataka elects 28 members to the Lok Sabha and has 12 Rajya Sabha seats, reflecting its population share.

questions.question: The Karnataka Lokayukta is an institution established to investigate
options: Corruption and maladministration by public servants
questions.explanation: The Lokayukta inquires into allegations of corruption and maladministration against public servants. Water disputes go to tribunals constituted under central law.

questions.question: The Kaveri water dispute primarily involves Karnataka and which other state?
questions.explanation: The long-running Kaveri dispute is chiefly between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, with Kerala and Puducherry also parties. The Krishna dispute involves Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh instead.

questions.question: Yakshagana, a traditional dance-drama, belongs chiefly to which part of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is performed mainly in the coastal and Malnad districts, combining dance, music and elaborate costume to tell epic stories.

questions.question: The Vachana literary tradition of Kannada is associated with which twelfth-century reform movement?
questions.explanation: Vachanas are terse prose-poems by Basavanna and other sharanas of the Lingayat movement, rejecting caste and ritual. They are a landmark of Kannada literature.

questions.question: Basavanna, the social reformer and Vachana poet, served as a minister in whose court?
questions.explanation: Basavanna was a minister in the court of the Kalachuri king Bijjala at Kalyana. Vishnuvardhana was an earlier Hoysala ruler.

questions.question: How many Kannada writers have received the Jnanpith Award, the highest literary honour in India?
questions.explanation: Kannada has eight Jnanpith laureates, the joint highest for any Indian language, beginning with K. V. Puttappa and including Masti, Bendre and U. R. Ananthamurthy.

questions.question: Purandara Dasa, born in Karnataka, is revered as the father of which musical tradition?
questions.explanation: Purandara Dasa systematised the teaching of Carnatic music and is called its Pitamaha. He composed extensively in Kannada as part of the Haridasa movement.

questions.question: Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani vocalist born in Karnataka, belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Bhimsen Joshi was the foremost exponent of the Kirana gharana and received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

questions.question: Bengaluru is known as the Silicon Valley of India chiefly because of which industry?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is India's largest IT export centre, hosting software and services firms alongside aerospace and defence research establishments.

questions.question: Which crop is Karnataka the largest producer of in India?
questions.explanation: Karnataka produces the bulk of India's coffee, centred on Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan. Wheat and jute belong to the northern and eastern states.

questions.question: Karnataka is India's leading producer of which mineral used in the aerospace industry?
questions.explanation: Karnataka leads India in gold production, with Hutti in Raichur district the main working mine. India has no significant petroleum output from the state.

questions.question: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, India's main aircraft manufacturer, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: HAL is headquartered at Bengaluru, though it operates divisions at Nashik, Kanpur and elsewhere.

questions.question: Nagarhole National Park is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Nagarhole is officially the Rajiv Gandhi National Park, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve alongside Bandipur.

questions.question: What is the state animal of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Indian elephant is the state animal and the Indian roller the state bird. Karnataka holds one of India's largest wild elephant populations.

questions.question: Ranganathittu, a well-known bird sanctuary in Karnataka, lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary sits on islets in the Kaveri near Srirangapatna in Mandya district.

questions.question: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site primarily for which value?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats were listed for their exceptional biodiversity and high levels of endemism, being one of the world's recognised hotspots.

questions.question: The Western Ganga dynasty ruled southern Karnataka from which early capital?
questions.explanation: The Western Gangas ruled from Talakadu on the Kaveri, having earlier used Kolar. Banavasi was the Kadamba capital and Manyakheta the Rashtrakuta one.

questions.question: Which Hoysala king is credited with commissioning the Chennakeshava temple at Belur?
questions.explanation: Vishnuvardhana commissioned the Chennakeshava temple around 1117 CE, traditionally to mark a victory over the Cholas. Ballala II ruled later at the dynasty's peak.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka under the guidance of which sage?
questions.explanation: Vidyaranya, a Sringeri seer, is traditionally credited with guiding the founding of Vijayanagara in 1336. Basavanna led the earlier Lingayat movement and Madhvacharya founded Dvaita philosophy.

questions.question: Which Adil Shahi ruler built the Gol Gumbaz at Vijayapura?
questions.explanation: The Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah, completed in 1656 and famed for its whispering gallery. Ibrahim Adil Shah II built the nearby Ibrahim Rauza.

questions.question: The Mysore kingdom was restored to the Wadiyars in 1799 after the defeat of which ruler?
questions.explanation: After Tipu Sultan died at Srirangapatna in 1799, the British restored the Wadiyar line under a subsidiary alliance, installing the child Krishnaraja Wadiyar III.

questions.question: Sangolli Rayanna, a Karnataka freedom fighter, fought the British on behalf of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Sangolli Rayanna was a commander under Rani Chennamma of Kittur and continued guerrilla resistance after her defeat, until he was captured and hanged in 1831.

questions.question: The Chalukya capital Badami is famous for which architectural feature?
questions.explanation: Badami is known for its four rock-cut cave temples carved into sandstone cliffs. Soapstone carving is Hoysala, and the Bahubali monolith is at Shravanabelagola.

questions.question: Which Karnataka site preserves Ashokan rock edicts?
questions.explanation: Minor rock edicts of Ashoka survive at Brahmagiri and other sites in Chitradurga district, marking the Mauryan reach into the south.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled from Kalyani and patronised the Vachana movement in its later years?
questions.explanation: The Western or Kalyani Chalukyas ruled from Basavakalyan, and it was under their Kalachuri successors that Basavanna's Vachana movement flourished.

questions.question: How many Rajya Sabha seats does Karnataka have?
questions.explanation: Karnataka elects 12 members to the Rajya Sabha, alongside its 28 Lok Sabha seats.

questions.question: The Karnataka Legislative Assembly has how many elected members?
questions.explanation: The Vidhana Sabha has 224 elected constituencies. The Legislative Council, the upper house, is much smaller and partly indirectly elected.

questions.question: Under which Article can Parliament create a new state by altering the boundaries of an existing one?
questions.explanation: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new states and alter boundaries, names and areas. Article 2 covers admitting new states into the Union.

questions.question: Which body recommended the reorganisation of Indian states on linguistic lines in 1955?
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission under Fazl Ali reported in 1955, leading to the 1956 Act that enlarged Mysore State. The earlier Dhar Commission had advised against linguistic reorganisation.

questions.question: Panchayat elections in Karnataka are conducted by which body?
questions.explanation: Article 243K vests panchayat and municipal elections in a State Election Commission. The Election Commission of India handles Parliament and the state legislature only.

questions.question: The Kali river of Karnataka flows through which district before reaching the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Kali rises in the Western Ghats and reaches the sea at Karwar in Uttara Kannada, and is dammed at Supa for hydroelectricity.

questions.question: Which is the largest lake in Karnataka by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Almatti reservoir on the Krishna is the largest water body in the state. Ulsoor and Hebbal are small urban lakes in Bengaluru.

questions.question: The Linganamakki dam is built across which river?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki impounds the Sharavathi in Shivamogga district and feeds the hydroelectric station below Jog Falls.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district borders both Goa and Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Belagavi district touches both Maharashtra to the north and Goa to the west. Bidar borders Maharashtra and Telangana instead.

questions.question: The Deccan plateau of Karnataka slopes generally in which direction?
questions.explanation: The plateau tilts east, which is why the Krishna, Kaveri and Tungabhadra flow east to the Bay of Bengal while only short rivers run west off the Ghats.

questions.question: Which soil type dominates the Malnad region of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Heavy rainfall in the Malnad leaches silica away and leaves iron-rich laterite. Black cotton soil dominates the drier northern plains instead.

questions.question: Mangaluru port handles a large share of which export from Karnataka?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port is the state's major seaport, historically shipping iron ore, coffee, cashew and granite.

questions.question: Which Karnataka dance form is performed by women balancing a decorated pot, associated with temple festivals?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's folk repertoire includes Dollu Kunitha with drums and Kolata with sticks. Kathakali is from Kerala and Odissi from Odisha.

questions.question: Which Kannada writer wrote 'Samskara', later made into an award-winning film?
questions.explanation: U. R. Ananthamurthy wrote Samskara in 1965. Girish Karnad acted in the film adaptation but wrote plays such as Tughlaq and Hayavadana.

questions.question: Shivaram Karanth, a Jnanpith laureate from Karnataka, is especially associated with reviving which art form?
questions.explanation: Shivaram Karanth experimented with and revived Yakshagana, the coastal dance-drama, alongside his novels and encyclopaedic writing.

questions.question: Which festival marks the Karnataka state formation day on 1 November?
questions.explanation: Kannada Rajyotsava marks the formation of the state in 1956. Ugadi is the Kannada new year and Dasara the Mysuru royal festival.

questions.question: The Sringeri Sharada Peetham was established by which philosopher?
questions.explanation: Adi Shankara established the Sringeri matha in Chikkamagaluru as one of his four cardinal seats. Madhvacharya founded the Udupi tradition instead.

questions.question: Udupi is associated with which philosopher and the Krishna temple he founded?
questions.explanation: Madhvacharya, founder of the Dvaita school, established the Udupi Krishna temple and its eight mathas.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district leads in sericulture, the rearing of silkworms?
questions.explanation: Ramanagara hosts one of Asia's largest silk cocoon markets, and Karnataka is India's leading silk producer.

questions.question: The Bhadravathi steel plant in Karnataka is associated with which name?
questions.explanation: The Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant at Bhadravathi was founded during the Mysore state's industrialisation and later named for M. Visvesvaraya.

questions.question: M. Visvesvaraya, the engineer honoured on Engineers' Day, served Mysore in which office?
questions.explanation: Visvesvaraya was Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1918 and oversaw the Krishna Raja Sagara dam and the state's industrial expansion.

questions.question: Which spice is widely intercropped with coffee in Kodagu and Chikkamagaluru?
questions.explanation: Black pepper vines are trained up the shade trees of coffee estates, making it a major Karnataka spice. Saffron is a Kashmir crop and cumin largely Gujarat and Rajasthan.

questions.question: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, a tiger reserve, lies in which part of Karnataka?
options: The Malnad in Chikkamagaluru and Shivamogga
questions.explanation: Bhadra straddles Chikkamagaluru and Shivamogga in the Malnad, and was among the earliest reserves to complete a voluntary village relocation.

questions.question: Which Karnataka bird sanctuary near Gadag is known for wintering waterfowl?
questions.explanation: Magadi in Gadag district hosts large numbers of migratory bar-headed geese each winter. Ranganathittu is on the Kaveri near Srirangapatna.

questions.question: What is the state flower of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The lotus is Karnataka's state flower, alongside the elephant as state animal, the Indian roller as state bird and sandalwood as state tree.

questions.question: Sandalwood, the state tree of Karnataka, is protected because of what pressure?
options: Illegal felling for its heartwood oil
questions.explanation: Sandalwood's aromatic heartwood makes mature trees valuable enough to attract smuggling, which is why cutting has long been regulated in the state.

questions.question: The Indian Institute of Science, India's premier research institute, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: IISc was founded at Bengaluru in 1909 with support from Jamsetji Tata and the Mysore royal family.

questions.question: ISRO's satellite manufacturing centre, U R Rao Satellite Centre, is in which city?
questions.explanation: The U R Rao Satellite Centre at Bengaluru builds ISRO's satellites. Launch vehicles come from Thiruvananthapuram and launches from Sriharikota.

questions.question: C. N. R. Rao, a Bharat Ratna recipient based in Karnataka, works in which field?
questions.explanation: C. N. R. Rao is a solid state and materials chemist and received the Bharat Ratna in 2014.

questions.question: The Karnataka High Court's benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi were created to serve which need?
options: Access to justice for the northern districts
questions.explanation: The circuit benches were established so litigants in northern Karnataka would not have to travel to Bengaluru for High Court matters.

questions.question: Which pass connects the coastal plain to the Bengaluru plateau along the Shiradi route?
questions.explanation: Shiradi Ghat carries the Mangaluru-Bengaluru route through the Western Ghats. Nathu La, Zoji La and Rohtang are Himalayan passes.

questions.question: The Nolamba dynasty of Karnataka ruled as feudatories of which larger power?
options: The Western Gangas and later the Rashtrakutas
questions.explanation: The Nolambas of the Tumakuru and Chitradurga region ruled as subordinates of the Gangas, Rashtrakutas and Chalukyas in turn.

questions.question: Which Kannada poet is known as Adikavi, the first poet?
questions.explanation: Pampa, author of Vikramarjuna Vijaya and Adipurana, is called Adikavi. Ranna and Ponna complete the ratnatraya, the three gems of old Kannada.

questions.question: The Bahmani Sultanate had one of its capitals in which Karnataka city?
questions.explanation: The Bahmanis moved their capital from Gulbarga to Bidar, where the fort and the Mahmud Gawan madrasa still stand.

questions.question: Mahmud Gawan, remembered for a madrasa at Bidar, served the Bahmani state as
questions.explanation: Mahmud Gawan was the Bahmani prime minister and a patron of learning, whose madrasa at Bidar survives in part.

questions.question: The Kadamba dynasty was founded by whom, according to tradition?
questions.explanation: Mayurasharma founded the Kadambas at Banavasi in the fourth century, traditionally after being slighted at a Pallava court.

questions.question: Who led the Amara Sullia and Kodagu uprising against the British in 1837?
questions.explanation: The 1837 Amara Sullia revolt in the Kodagu and Dakshina Kannada region briefly captured Mangaluru before being suppressed.

questions.question: Which Karnataka body hears appeals in revenue and land matters below the High Court?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Appellate Tribunal hears appeals in revenue and certain other matters, sitting above the Deputy Commissioner in that ladder.

questions.question: Recruitment to Karnataka's state civil services is conducted by
questions.explanation: KPSC conducts the state civil service examinations. UPSC handles the all-India services and central posts.

questions.question: Members of the Karnataka Legislative Council are chosen partly by which electorates?
options: Graduates, teachers, local authorities and the assembly
questions.explanation: A Legislative Council is composed of members elected by MLAs, local authorities, graduates and teachers, plus a share nominated by the Governor.

questions.question: Which Article empowers a state to have a Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a state Legislative Council on a resolution of that state's assembly.

questions.question: The Bhima river, a major tributary of the Krishna, enters Karnataka from which state?
questions.explanation: The Bhima rises in Maharashtra's Bhimashankar hills and flows through northern Karnataka before joining the Krishna.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district is known for its granite and dimensional stone quarries?
options: Ilkal in Bagalkot and surrounding areas
questions.explanation: Northern Karnataka around Ilkal and Bagalkot is a major granite and building-stone region, quite unlike the laterite-rich coast.

questions.question: Which Karnataka river joins the Krishna near Raichur after flowing past Hampi?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra flows past Hampi and joins the Krishna near Raichur, watering the doab between the two rivers.

questions.question: The Raichur doab lies between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: A doab is the land between two rivers, and the Raichur doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra, long fought over by Vijayanagara and the Sultanates.

questions.question: Which Karnataka coastal district is known for its fishing harbour at Malpe?
questions.explanation: Malpe near Udupi is one of Karnataka's largest fishing harbours, and the departure point for St Mary's Island.

questions.question: Which classical Kannada text on grammar and poetics survives from the ninth century?
questions.explanation: Kavirajamarga, attributed to the Rashtrakuta court, is the earliest available Kannada literary work and discusses poetics and the Kannada country.

questions.question: Kuvempu, the first Kannada Jnanpith laureate, wrote which epic in blank verse?
questions.explanation: Kuvempu's Sri Ramayana Darshanam earned him the Jnanpith in 1967. He also wrote the state anthem, Jaya Bharata Jananiya Tanujate.

questions.question: Which Kannada writer received the Jnanpith for a body of work including 'Yayati' style historical drama and is known for Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Girish Karnad, a Jnanpith laureate, wrote Tughlaq, Hayavadana and Yayati. Kambara and Bendre are separate laureates with their own bodies of work.

questions.question: D. R. Bendre, a Jnanpith winner, wrote principally in which form?
questions.explanation: Bendre, who wrote under the name Ambikatanayadatta, is celebrated for lyric poetry in the Dharwad Kannada idiom.

questions.question: Which Karnataka temple town is the seat of the Vaishnava saint Ramanuja's long exile?
questions.explanation: Ramanuja spent years at Melukote in Mandya district, where the Cheluvanarayana temple and the Vairamudi festival remain associated with him.

questions.question: Which Karnataka institution is India's principal centre for aerospace research alongside HAL?
questions.explanation: NAL at Bengaluru is a CSIR laboratory working on civil aircraft and aerospace research, close to HAL and the defence cluster.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district produces the largest share of the state's arecanut?
questions.explanation: Arecanut is concentrated in the Malnad districts of Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Dakshina Kannada, where rainfall is high.

questions.question: Karnataka's Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001 primarily because
options: Mining had become uneconomic at increasing depth
The gold ran out completely overnight
The site was flooded by a dam
questions.explanation: KGF reached extreme depths where extraction costs exceeded the value recovered, and Bharat Gold Mines was wound up in 2001.

questions.question: Which Karnataka city is the centre of the state's garment export industry?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru hosts a large ready-made garment manufacturing and export sector alongside its IT industry.

questions.question: Which Karnataka national park adjoins Bandipur and Nagarhole to form part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve?
options: Mudumalai lies across the border in Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: Bandipur and Nagarhole in Karnataka adjoin Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu and Wayanad in Kerala within the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

questions.question: Kudremukh National Park was the subject of a long dispute over which activity?
options: Iron ore mining inside the park
questions.explanation: Iron ore mining inside Kudremukh was phased out after litigation over its impact on the Bhadra catchment and the shola-grassland ecosystem.

questions.question: Which bird is the state bird of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Indian roller, or neelakanta, is the state bird. The peacock is the national bird.

questions.question: Kokkarebellur in Mandya district is known for the community protection of which birds?
questions.explanation: Villagers at Kokkarebellur have long protected nesting painted storks and spot-billed pelicans, treating them as bringing good fortune.

questions.question: Which Karnataka institution is India's national centre for biological sciences research under TIFR?
questions.explanation: The National Centre for Biological Sciences at Bengaluru is part of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

questions.question: The Indian Deep Space Network, which tracks ISRO's interplanetary missions, is located near which Karnataka town?
questions.explanation: The Indian Deep Space Network antennas at Byalalu tracked Chandrayaan and the Mars Orbiter Mission.

questions.question: Raman Research Institute, founded by C. V. Raman, is in which city?
questions.explanation: C. V. Raman founded the Raman Research Institute at Bengaluru in 1948 after his years at IISc. His Nobel-winning work was done earlier in Kolkata.

questions.question: Karnataka's anti-corruption body created in 1984 to inquire into public servants' conduct is the
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Lokayukta was constituted in 1984 and has been among the more prominent state anti-corruption institutions.

questions.question: Which is the westernmost point of Karnataka's coastline district-wise?
questions.explanation: Uttara Kannada occupies the northern part of Karnataka's coast, adjoining Goa. Kolar, Bidar and Chamarajanagar are all inland.

questions.question: Which Karnataka festival involves decorated bulls and is celebrated at harvest time?
options: Kambala and Sankranti bull traditions of the coast and plains
questions.explanation: Coastal Karnataka holds Kambala buffalo races, and Sankranti brings cattle decoration across the state. Onam and Bihu belong to Kerala and Assam.

questions.question: Which Karnataka fort city was the Adil Shahi capital?
questions.explanation: Vijayapura, formerly Bijapur, was the Adil Shahi capital and holds the Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza. Bidar was the Bahmani and later Barid Shahi capital.

questions.question: Which Karnataka board markets the state's silk under a well-known brand?
questions.explanation: KSIC manufactures and markets Mysore Silk. The Coffee Board is a central body headquartered in Bengaluru but deals with coffee.

questions.question: The Western Ghats in Karnataka are a source region for which two major east-flowing rivers?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri rises in Kodagu and the Tunga and Bhadra in Chikkamagaluru, all in the Karnataka Ghats, and all flow east.

questions.question: Which Bengaluru institution designs India's military aircraft engines and gas turbines?
questions.explanation: GTRE, a DRDO laboratory in Bengaluru, works on aero gas turbine engines including the Kaveri programme.

questions.question: Which official heads the administration of a Zilla Panchayat in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: A Chief Executive Officer, usually an IAS officer, heads the Zilla Panchayat administration alongside the elected president.

questions.question: St Mary's Island off the Karnataka coast is geologically notable for
questions.explanation: The islands off Malpe show hexagonal columnar basalt, a national geological monument linked to the rifting of Madagascar from India.
